value.body: Earning by working for yourself — a trade or service (electrical work, tailoring, mobile repair, beauty services), a shop, farm-linked work, freelancing, or a registered startup. Many people begin small, often within a family business, and grow over time.

items.note: All ages, usual status; includes helpers in family enterprises

items.label: DPIIT-recognised startups
items.source: Lok Sabha reply, Ministry of Commerce (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: There is no exam or minimum qualification. It suits people with a skill, a family business or a clear local need to serve, and some tolerance for uneven income. Free online Udyam registration formalises a small business and is needed for many MSME schemes; government credit schemes such as PM Mudra Yojana and PMEGP lend to small units, subject to eligibility.

value.title: At a glance
items: Income is irregular, especially in the first years; savings or family support often carry the gap.
Most self-employed people in India run very small units; registered startups are a much narrower slice.
A skill certificate (ITI or a short course) can add credibility for trades such as electrical or plumbing work.
Registrations, GST (above turnover thresholds) and basic bookkeeping are part of running a business.

value.title: Share of workers who are self-employed
value.note: Usual status, all India. Self-employment includes own-account work, employers and unpaid family helpers, so it is broader than starting a business. The 2022-23 figure comes from a secondary summary.
